transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately I feel like how I see myself depends almost completely on what I weigh or how my body looks. It’s just become this constant thing in my head, and my wife gently suggested I should come in and talk to someone about it.

Do you ever feel like you lose control over your eating, such as consuming a very large amount of food in a short time, and do you ever feel the need to use methods like vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise to manage your weight?

Yes, when I get home late, it feels like a switch flips and I'll just stand at the counter eating leftovers, cereal, or peanut butter until I'm uncomfortably full and can't seem to stop. To make up for it, I'll try to "reset" by starving myself on coffee the next day, going on punishingly long walks, or sometimes even making myself throw up in the bathroom with the shower running so my family doesn't hear.
How often, on average, do these episodes of binge eating and subsequent purging or compensatory behaviors occur each week?

This has become almost a routine, happening at least once or twice a week. It really started a few months after our second baby was born, where I'll have a late-night blowout eating episode and then either starve myself or make myself throw up the next day to try to undo it.
When you engage in these behaviors, is your primary focus on purging through vomiting and laxatives, or are you primarily using restrictive fasting and excessive exercise to compensate?

Honestly, I use both methods depending on how bad the night was. On the nights I really overdo it, I'll resort to making myself throw up in the bathroom with the shower running so no one hears. Other times, I try to compensate by living on just coffee and maybe an apple, or forcing myself to go on long, punishing walks after my closing shift.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa, characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, fasting, and excessive exercise) to prevent weight gain. The self-evaluation is also unduly influenced by body shape and weight.
